findings.title: A lost acknowledgement followed by another answer double-counts flashcard rewards
findings.problem: Flashcard deduplication depends on the complete local and server reward objects being equal. Once the student answers another question, those objects differ even though both snapshots contain the same already-committed flashcard grade. Reconciliation then adds that grade's XP and card count twice. The total-XP calculation in reconcileProgress has the same whole-snapshot equality dependency.
findings.failure_scenario: Start from an acknowledged 0-XP baseline. Grade one card Good: the server commits 5 XP, but its response is lost. Before retrying, answer a new difficulty-1 question correctly, producing a local snapshot with 15 XP. On the revision conflict, reconciliation calculates 10 replayed question XP plus 5 local card XP plus 5 server card XP, saving 20 XP and two reviewed cards instead of 15 XP and one card. The existing lost-acknowledgement test only retries identical snapshots, so it misses this case.
findings.fix: Assign stable operation IDs to flashcard grades and undos, and merge each operation once rather than inferring duplication from whole-object equality. Add a regression that commits a grade without acknowledging it, advances the local snapshot with a question answer, and then retries through reconciliation.

findings.title: A stale reconciled save advances the baseline without updating local progress
findings.problem: store.set assigns a conflict-merged blob to both acceptedBlob and loadedBaseline before returning. If a newer snapshot was queued while that write was running, createSaveQueue marks the response stale and the autosave callback skips applyBlob. The queued snapshot therefore lacks the remote changes, but its next reconciliation treats those changes as part of its baseline. Missing remote XP becomes a negative local delta and is subtracted from the saved total.
findings.failure_scenario: Both devices start at 0 XP. Another device saves answer A for 10 XP. This device answers B for 10 XP; its save conflicts and writes the merged A+B snapshot for 20 XP. While that save's response is pending, this device answers C, queuing its still-local B+C snapshot for 20 XP. The A+B response is discarded as stale, but loadedBaseline has already become A+B. Saving B+C then preserves all three log rows while saving only 20 XP instead of 30 XP.
findings.fix: Keep the baseline associated with the local snapshot separate from the acknowledged merged server blob. Do not advance that local baseline to a reconciliation that was never applied to local state, or explicitly fold the remote delta into subsequent queued snapshots. Add an adapter-level regression with a held conflict-write response and a second answer before acknowledgement.

findings.title: Conflict merging overwrites another device's legacy-answer resolution
findings.problem: When mergeLogs finds the same attempt or legacy occurrence on both sides, it always keeps the local row. It does not consult the baseline to distinguish a local edit from an unchanged stale copy. Consequently, a remote source/key correction is erased by an unrelated local save.
findings.failure_scenario: Two devices load an unresolved legacy miss. Device A identifies it as builtin:7 and saves its source/key. Device B has not changed that log row; it only changes the theme. B's revision conflict fetches A's resolved row, but sameLegacyOccurrence matches it to B's old unresolved row and out.push(localLog[match]) restores the unresolved version. The next save deletes the recorded provenance and puts the miss back into unresolved review.
findings.fix: Make matched-row merging baseline-aware: preserve the server row when the local occurrence is unchanged from the baseline, and apply local identity changes only when that occurrence was actually edited locally. Add the reverse of the existing local-resolution test: remote resolution plus an unrelated local setting change must retain the remote source and key.

assessment: Request changes. I found three concrete persistence defects that can duplicate rewards, lose remote XP, or erase saved answer provenance. The new tests do not cover these evolving-snapshot conflict paths. I could not run the suite from the supplied material.
